title: Spicy Paneer Thecha: The High-Protein Maharashtrian Snack Taking Over Indian Kitchens
excerpt: This dietician-approved recipe packs nearly 60 grams of protein per batch, takes under 30 minutes, and has earned celebrity fans from Malaika Arora to fitness influencers.
body:
• Paneer thecha is a Maharashtrian-style dish that coats paneer cubes in a coarse paste of roasted peanuts, green chillies, garlic, and fresh coriander.
  • A full batch delivers approximately 58 grams of protein, making it one of the most protein-dense vegetarian snacks in Indian cuisine.
  • The recipe takes under 30 minutes, requires no exotic ingredients, and works as a starter, evening snack, or high-protein side dish.
  • Dieticians recommend it as a guilt-free weight-loss snack due to its high satiety factor and clean ingredient profile.

What Is Paneer Thecha?

Thecha is a fiery Maharashtrian condiment traditionally made by pounding green chillies, garlic, and peanuts in a mortar and pestle — the rough, rustic texture is the whole point. Paneer thecha takes that bold, earthy chutney and turns it into a coating for pan-fried paneer cubes, creating a snack that hits every note: spicy, smoky, crunchy, and satisfying.

The dish gained mainstream popularity after Bollywood actress Malaika Arora spotlighted it as one of her favourite foods at her Mumbai restaurant Scarlett House, calling it both low in calories and high in protein. Since then, paneer thecha has exploded across Indian food social media, with dieticians and fitness influencers championing it as the rare Indian snack that is genuinely weight-loss friendly.

The Recipe

Ingredients

For the thecha: 8–10 garlic cloves, 4–5 spicy green chillies, one-third cup raw peanuts, one cup fresh coriander (leaves and stems), salt to taste, juice of half a lemon.

For the paneer: 250 grams paneer (cut into cubes or thick slabs), 1–2 tablespoons oil for shallow frying.

For serving: Sliced onions (lachha style), green chutney, lemon wedges.

Method

Step 1 — Dry roast the base: Heat a pan without oil. Add the peanuts, garlic cloves, and green chillies. Dry roast for 5–7 minutes, stirring frequently, until the peanuts turn golden and the chillies blister. The kitchen should smell rustic and smoky — that is the signal they are ready.

Step 2 — Make the thecha: Transfer the roasted peanuts, garlic, and chillies to a mortar and pestle (or a mixer grinder on pulse). Add the fresh coriander, salt, and lemon juice. Crush to a coarse, chunky paste — not a smooth puree. The texture should be rough and grainy.

Step 3 — Coat and cook the paneer: Generously coat the paneer cubes with the prepared thecha, pressing it on so it sticks. Heat a teaspoon of oil in a non-stick pan and shallow fry the coated paneer on medium heat until golden and crisp on all sides, about 2–3 minutes per side.

Step 4 — Serve hot: Plate the paneer thecha with sliced onions, green chutney, and lemon wedges on the side. It pairs beautifully with roti, as a rice bowl topping, or simply eaten on its own as a high-protein snack.

"Real paneer will break and crumble like khoya. Paneer made from detergent or urea will stretch like rubber or feel too hard."

— FSDA advisory on identifying adulterated paneer

The Nutrition Case

The protein math is hard to argue with. A batch made with 200 grams of paneer delivers roughly 36 grams of protein from the paneer alone. Add 13 grams from the peanuts, 4 grams from yogurt (if using a dip), and smaller contributions from sesame seeds and other ingredients, and you are looking at approximately 58 grams of total protein per full recipe — or about 14–15 grams per serving if divided into four portions.

For vegetarians managing their protein intake, those are elite numbers from a single snack. Paneer thecha avoids the heavy gravies and excess oil that make many Indian paneer dishes calorie bombs, while the peanuts provide healthy fats and the chillies offer a metabolic boost.

Tips for the Best Results

Use fresh, firm paneer — block paneer works better than crumbled. If the thecha is too spicy, reduce the green chillies and add a tablespoon of roasted sesame seeds for nuttiness without heat. For an air fryer version, coat the paneer and air fry at 165°C for about 8 minutes. And for a tangy twist, replace the lemon juice with two tablespoons of grated raw mango.
